standard: CCSS 8.G.B.7: Apply the Pythagorean theorem to determine unknown side lengths in right triangles in real-world and mathematical problems in two and three dimensions.
source: Original content written for Pip (no third-party text copied); aligned to CCSS 8.G.B.7.
attribution: Pip team, original. Common Core standards are cited for alignment only.
in_scope: which side of a right triangle is the long side
a² + b² = c² as the rule people use
a skatepark shortcut across a corner
out_of_scope: the converse (is this corner a right angle)

look_fors: Says the long side c is across from the right angle (one sentence is enough)
Says it is the longest side (the biggest angle faces the longest side)
May point at a corner of a skatepark and the straight shortcut across
probe_ladder: why is that wrong? the long side should be the two short sides put together.
which side of a right triangle is the longest, and where is it?
is there a special name for the side that never touches the square corner?
then the long side is the two short sides put together, even for a skinny triangle. that's what my rule says.
concrete: what if i draw a right triangle and walk straight across from the corner, which side is that?
connections: so the long side is like the shortcut straight across a skatepark corner?
concepts.friend_nudge: My cousin said the long side is the one that never touches the square corner…? I don't know why that matters.
concepts.aha: ohh the long one is the side across from the corner.

look_fors: Says the two short sides squared add up to the long side squared
Accepts that it is a theorem; 'that's just the theorem' counts as a full reason
probe_ladder: what do we do with the two short sides to get the long one?
i'll guess you just add them. is that right?
what's the rule people use for the long side?
then a long side of 3 + 4 is 7, longer than any walk. that's what my rule says.
concrete: what if i draw a square on each side of a 3-4-5 triangle, how many tiles in each?
connections: so it's like two small squares of floor tiles filling one big square?
concepts.friend_nudge: My neighbor said it's about squares on the sides…? I'm not sure which ones.
concepts.aha: ok so the two small squares fill the big one.

look_fors: Uses the rule on legs 3 and 4: 9 + 16 = 25, so c = 5
Applies it to a new pair of legs (6 and 8 give 10)
Says when it applies: right triangles only
probe_ladder: what's the long side of a right triangle with legs 3 and 4?
can you do one with legs 6 and 8?
then 6 + 8 = 14 is the long side. that's what my rule says.
concrete: what if the two short sides are 3 and 4, how long is the shortcut?
connections: so it's like walking 3 blocks and 4 blocks, but the shortcut goes straight across?
concepts.friend_nudge: Someone in my class said a 3 by 4 corner has a shortcut you can measure with a string…? I don't get how that helps.
concepts.aha: ok so you square both, add, and take the root.
